brief.md:1: # AT86RF233 SPI carrier board for ESP32-C6 host
brief.md:3: A minimal 2-layer carrier board that breaks out a Microchip AT86RF233-ZU
brief.md:4: 2.4 GHz O-QPSK transceiver over SPI to a host MCU. The host is an ESP32-C6
brief.md:5: (Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6 module, not populated on this board) which does not
brief.md:6: have native access to the AT86RF233's proprietary high-rate O-QPSK PHY
brief.md:7: modes. This board exists purely to give SPI/GPIO access to a real
brief.md:8: AT86RF233, so firmware can drive it into non-standard configurations
brief.md:9: (custom SFD value, non-standard OQPSK_DATA_RATE) to receive and transmit
brief.md:10: Sena Mesh (30K) and Cardo DMC packets.
brief.md:12: ## Scope
brief.md:14: - AT86RF233-ZU transceiver, QFN-32, with full basic application circuit
brief.md:15: from the datasheet (decoupling, DVDD/AVDD filtering, crystal, RESET,
brief.md:16: SLP_TR, IRQ).
brief.md:17: - 2.4 GHz chip antenna (or PCB inverted-F antenna if a suitable reference
brief.md:18: layout is available) with matching network per Microchip's reference
brief.md:19: design. Antenna feed must be a controlled-impedance 50 ohm trace.
brief.md:20: - SPI interface (MOSI, MISO, SCLK, /SEL) plus IRQ, RESET, and SLP_TR
brief.md:21: broken out to a 2.54mm pin header, pin-compatible in spirit with a
brief.md:22: Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6 wired by jumper wires (no XIAO on this board, no
brief.md:23: onboard MCU at all).
brief.md:24: - Power input: single 3.3V rail from an external source via the same
brief.md:25: header (board does not regulate its own power; host supplies 3.3V).
brief.md:26: - No battery, no charger, no display, no audio path on this board — those
brief.md:27: live on separate modules wired externally.
brief.md:28: - Test points on SPI lines and on the antenna feed for probing during
brief.md:29: bring-up.
brief.md:31: ## Explicit non-goals
brief.md:33: - No onboard ESP32 / microcontroller.
brief.md:34: - No onboard voltage regulation or battery management.
brief.md:35: - No audio codec, microphone, or speaker circuitry.
brief.md:36: - No enclosure or mechanical design.
brief.md:37: - Do not substitute a different 2.4 GHz transceiver family (must be
brief.md:38: AT86RF233-ZU specifically, not AT86RF231 or AT86RF212).
brief.md:40: ## Budgets
brief.md:42: - Board outline: fit within 25mm x 20mm if possible; smaller is fine.
brief.md:43: - Supply: single 3.3V rail, target current draw under 40mA average,
brief.md:44: peak under 20mA extra during TX per datasheet.
brief.md:45: - Layer count: 2 layers, standard 1.6mm FR4, unless the antenna matching
brief.md:46: network genuinely requires more layers to hit a controlled 50 ohm
brief.md:47: trace — flag this explicitly if so rather than silently going to 4
brief.md:48: layers.
brief.md:50: ## Reference material
brief.md:52: - Microchip AT86RF233 datasheet (Atmel-8351), section on the basic
brief.md:53: application schematic and PCB antenna reference layout.
brief.md:54: - Part number for the transceiver: AT86RF233-ZU.
brief.md:56: ## Deliverables
brief.md:58: - KiCad schematic and PCB layout, ERC/DRC clean.
brief.md:59: - Gerbers, drill files, and STEP model.
brief.md:60: - BOM with real, sourceable part numbers and datasheet references for
brief.md:61: every part, especially the antenna matching network components.
brief.md:62: - A short bring-up note describing how to verify SPI communication by
brief.md:63: reading the AT86RF233 PART_NUM (expect 0x0b) and VERSION_NUM
brief.md:64: (expect 0x01 or 0x02) registers before anything else is trusted.

# AT86RF233 SPI Carrier Board Specification

## Device

A minimal 2-layer carrier board provides SPI/GPIO access to a Microchip AT86RF233-ZU 2.4 GHz O-QPSK transceiver from an externally wired Seeed XIAO ESP32-C6 host. The XIAO is not populated on this board; firmware uses the AT86RF233 proprietary configuration registers for Sena Mesh (30K) and Cardo DMC experiments.

## Required circuitry

- U1 shall be an AT86RF233-ZU in QFN-32; AT86RF231, AT86RF212, and other transceiver families are forbidden.
- The schematic shall implement the datasheet basic application circuit: decoupling, DVDD/AVDD filtering, crystal, RESET, SLP_TR, and IRQ.
- A 2.4 GHz chip antenna or a PCB inverted-F antenna with a suitable reference layout shall use the Microchip reference matching network.
- The antenna feed shall be controlled impedance, 50 ohm.
- A 2.54 mm header shall expose 3V3, GND, MOSI, MISO, SCLK, /SEL, IRQ, RESET, and SLP_TR.
- Test points shall be present on MOSI, MISO, SCLK, /SEL, and the antenna feed.

## Constraints and budgets

| Constraint | Requirement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Supply | One externally supplied 3.3 V rail only; no onboard regulator | Stated |
| Average current | Less than 40 mA target | Stated |
| TX incremental peak current | Less than 20 mA additional during TX | Stated |
| Board outline | At most 25 mm x 20 mm where practicable; smaller is acceptable | Stated |
| Stackup | Two layers, standard 1.6 mm FR-4 | Stated |
| RF exception | More than two layers is permitted only when required to realize the 50 ohm antenna feed/matching network, and must be explicitly flagged | Stated |
| Copper weight | 1 oz copper assumed for initial 50 ohm impedance calculation; confirm against the selected fabricator stackup before layout release | ASSUMED |
| Host logic level | Header SPI/GPIO signals are 3.3 V logic only; no level shifting is included | ASSUMED |

## Explicit exclusions

No onboard ESP32 or other MCU, voltage regulation, battery management, charger, audio codec, microphone, speaker, enclosure, or mechanical product design is in scope.

## Deliverables

- KiCad schematic and PCB, ERC/DRC clean.
- Gerbers, drill files, DXF outline, and STEP model.
- BOM with real sourceable part numbers and datasheet references, including RF matching components.
- Bring-up note: first read `PART_NUM` (expect `0x0b`) and `VERSION_NUM` (expect `0x01` or `0x02`) over SPI before trusting further operation.

## References

- Microchip AT86RF233 datasheet, Atmel-8351: basic application schematic and PCB antenna reference layout.
- Product brief: `brief.md`.

## Decisions

- Use the datasheet reference RF topology and retain a two-layer board target; this minimizes implementation risk while preserving the stated size and cost goal.
